subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Haloform reaction of aryl methyl ketone
stem:
For the following reaction sequence, choose the correct option:

Benzene \(\xrightarrow[\text{ii. NaOCl}]{\text{i. CH}_3\text{COCl, AlCl}_3}\) P + Q
options: If P is the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid, Q is a primary alcohol.
P and Q are aromatic compounds.
If P gives a carboxylic acid on acidification, Q gives a poisonous gas on exposure to air and light.
Both P and Q are carbonyl compounds.
solution: Benzene with CH3COCl/AlCl3 gives acetophenone (Friedel-Crafts acylation). Acetophenone with NaOCl (haloform reaction) gives sodium benzoate (P) + CHCl3 (Q). P on acidification gives benzoic acid (COOH). CHCl3 on exposure to air and light gives phosgene COCl2, a poisonous gas.

The correct order of solubility of the given salts in water at 298 K is

| Salt | \(K_{sp}\) at 298 K |
|---|---|
| AgBr | \(5.0 \times 10^{-13}\) |
| \(\text{Zn(OH)}_2\) | \(1.0 \times 10^{-15}\) |
| \(\text{Hg}_2\text{Cl}_2\) | \(1.3 \times 10^{-18}\) |
solution: For AgBr (AX type): \(K_{sp} = S^2 \Rightarrow S_1 = \sqrt{5\times10^{-13}} = 7.1\times10^{-7}\) M. For \(\text{Zn(OH)}_2\) (\(AX_2\) type): \(K_{sp} = 4S^3 \Rightarrow S_2 = (1.0\times10^{-15}/4)^{1/3} = 6.3\times10^{-6}\) M. For \(\text{Hg}_2\text{Cl}_2\) (\(AX_2\) type): \(S_3 = (1.3\times10^{-18}/4)^{1/3} = 6.9\times10^{-7}\) M. Order of solubility: \(\text{Zn(OH)}_2 > \text{AgBr} > \text{Hg}_2\text{Cl}_2\).

subtopic: Ideal solutions and enthalpy/volume of mixing
stem:
Assertion A: For an ideal solution formed by mixing liquids P and Q, \(\Delta_{mix} H = 0\) and \(\Delta_{mix} V = 0\)
Reason R: No interactions occur between P and Q
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
solution: If the intermolecular attractive forces between the P–P and Q–Q are nearly equal to those between P–Q, this leads to the formation of ideal solution. As interactions remain nearly same, therefore \(\Delta H_{mix} = 0\) and \(\Delta V_{mix} = 0\). Hence, Assertion is correct and Reason is incorrect.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
For a salt XY, which is a strong electrolyte, the plot of \(\Lambda_m\) versus \(\sqrt{c}\) has a slope of \(-90.0\) S cm\(^2\) mol\(^{-3/2}\) L\(^{1/2}\) at 298 K. At 0.01 M concentration of XY, the values of \(\Lambda_m\) is 145 S cm\(^2\) mol\(^{-1}\). The limiting molar conductivity of \(Y^{-}\) ion (\(\lambda^0_{Y^-}\), in S cm\(^2\) mol\(^{-1}\)) at 298 K will be
(Given \(\lambda^0_{X^+} = 74.0\) S cm\(^2\) mol\(^{-1}\))
solution: For XY, Debye-Huckel-Onsager equation: \(\Lambda_M = \Lambda_M^0 - A\sqrt{c}\). Slope \(-A = -90\), so A = 90. At C = 0.01 M, \(\Lambda_M = 145\): \(145 = \Lambda_M^0 - 90\times\sqrt{10^{-2}} = \Lambda_M^0 - 9\), so \(\Lambda_M^0 = 154\) S cm\(^2\) mol\(^{-1}\). \(\Lambda_M^0(XY) = \lambda^0(X^+) + \lambda^0(Y^-)\); \(154 = 74 + \lambda^0(Y^-)\), so \(\lambda^0(Y^-) = 80\) S cm\(^2\) mol\(^{-1}\).

subtopic: Reactions of halides with conc. H2SO4 and MnO2
stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : Heating NaCl with concentrated \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) and \(\text{MnO}_2\) results in oxidation of Mn.
Statement-II : Heating NaI with concentrated \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\) and \(\text{MnO}_2\) results in reduction of Mn.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.
solution: S-(I): \(4\text{NaCl} + \overset{+4}{\text{MnO}_2} + 4\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \overset{+2}{\text{MnCl}_2} + 4\text{NaHSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Cl}_2\). Mn is reduced (+4 to +2), not oxidised, so statement is wrong. S-(II): \(2\text{NaI} + \overset{+4}{\text{MnO}_2} + 4\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{I}_2(\uparrow) + \overset{+2}{\text{MnSO}_4} + \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\). Mn is reduced, statement is correct.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Carnot-type cycle - work and internal energy
stem:
Consider the reversible processes for 1.0 mol of an ideal gas as shown in the figure. Processes 1 (\(p_1,V_1,T_1 \rightarrow p_2,V_2,T_1\)) and 3 (\(p_3,V_3,T_2 \rightarrow p_4,V_4,T_2\)) are isothermal; processes 2 and 4 are adiabatic. \(w_1, w_2, w_3\) and \(w_4\) represent work done (in calories) in the processes 1, 2, 3 and 4, respectively; \(\Delta U_2\) and \(\Delta U_4\) are changes in the internal energy for the processes 2 and 4, respectively.
(use R = 2 cal K\(^{-1}\) mol\(^{-1}\))
The correct option is
solution: Process-1 is isothermal reversible: \(w_1 = -nRT\ln(V_f/V_i) = -1\times2\times T_1\ln(V_2/V_1) = -2T_1\ln(V_2/V_1)\). Process-3 is isothermal reversible: \(w_3 = -2T_2\ln(V_4/V_3)\). Therefore \(w_1 + w_3 = -2T_1\ln(V_2/V_1) - 2T_2\ln(V_4/V_3)\). Process-2 (adiabatic expansion): \(w_2 = \Delta U_2 = C_v(T_2 - T_1)\); Process-4 (adiabatic compression): \(w_4 = \Delta U_4 = -C_v(T_2 - T_1)\); so \(w_2 + w_4 = \Delta U_2 + \Delta U_4 = 0\).

stem: A protein undergoes reversible thermal denaturation from its initial state N to denatured state D according to \(N \rightleftharpoons D\). At 60 \(^\circ\)C, the concentrations of both N and D are equal at equilibrium, and the standard enthalpy change of denaturation is 666 kJ mol\(^{-1}\). The standard entropy change (\(\Delta S^\circ\) in kJ K\(^{-1}\) mol\(^{-1}\)) of the protein upon denaturation at 60\(^\circ\)C is closest to
solution: \(N \rightleftharpoons D\), \(K = [D]/[N] = 1\) (as [D] = [N] at equilibrium). \(\Delta G^\circ = -2.303 RT\log K = 0\) (as K = 1). \(\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ\); \(0 = 666 - 333\Delta S^\circ\); \(\Delta S^\circ = 666/333 = 2\) kJ K\(^{-1}\)mol\(^{-1}\).

Statement-II: cis-But-2-ene upon treatment with alkaline \(\text{KMnO}_4\) gives a product (Newman projection: front carbon with OH up and OH and Me, back carbon with H, H and Me).

subtopic: Stereochemistry from alkyne reduction and HBr addition
stem:
Consider the following reaction sequences and choose the correct option:
\(\text{Ph-C}\equiv\text{C-Me}\): with Na/liq. NH3 gives L (trans-alkene); L with HBr/benzoyl peroxide gives N. \(\text{Ph-C}\equiv\text{C-Me}\) with \(\text{H}_2\), Pd/C (Lindlar's Catalyst) gives K (cis-alkene); K with HBr gives M.
options: K and L are geometrical isomers.
M and N are geometrical isomers.
solution: \(\text{Ph-C}\equiv\text{C-Me}\) with Lindlar's catalyst gives cis-alkene K; with Na/liq. NH3 gives trans-alkene L. K and L are geometrical (cis-trans) isomers. K + HBr (Markovnikov) gives M = \(\text{Ph-CHBr-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3\); L + HBr/benzoyl peroxide (anti-Markovnikov) gives N = \(\text{Ph-CH}_2\text{-CHBr-CH}_3\).

A. Benzonitrile (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}\)) with \(\text{LiAlH}_4\)
B. Benzamide (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONH}_2\)) with KOH, \(\text{Br}_2\)
C. Nitrobenzene (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2\)) with \(\text{NaBH}_4\)

Statement-I : Oxidation of p-nitrotoluene with acidic \(\text{KMnO}_4\) gives an acid that is stronger than benzoic acid.
Statement-II : Reduction of p-nitrotoluene with Sn/HCl followed by neutralization gives an amine that is more basic than aniline.

stem: A 1 : 3 electrolyte in an aqueous solution is
solution: \([\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3 \Rightarrow [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^-\), giving 1 cation and 3 anions = 1 : 3 electrolyte.

subtopic: Radial nodes in orbital wavefunction plots
stem: Consider the schematic plots of orbital wavefunction (\(\psi_r\)) against distance (r) from the nucleus (four plots A, B, C, D). The figure representing two radial nodes in the orbital is
solution: In figure C, the curve is cutting the x-axis two times. Hence, it represents two nodes.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Order of polarity of organic compounds
stem:
Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of polarity
A. \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3\)
B. \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\)
C. \(\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3\)
D. \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Increasing order of polarity: \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3\) < \(\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3\) < \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}\) < \(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}\), i.e. A < C < B < D.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The highest occupied molecular orbital for \(\text{Ne}_2\) is
solution: \(\text{Ne}_2 \Rightarrow 20e^-\). MO configuration: \(\sigma1s^2 < \sigma^{*}1s^2 < \sigma2s^2 < \sigma^{*}2s^2 < \sigma2p_z^2 < \pi2p_x^2 = \pi2p_y^2 < \pi^{*}2p_x^2 = \pi^{*}2p_y^2 < \sigma^{*}2p_z^2\). The Highest Occupied Molecular Orbital (HOMO) is \(\sigma^{*}_{2p}\).
